We have many reagents. Need to identify three cations. Use systematic approach: test for groups: alkali metals (Na+, K+), alkaline earth (Ca2+, Sr2+, Ba2+), transition metals (Cu2+, Fe2+/3+, Ni2+, Co2+, Zn2+, Pb2+, etc), heavy metals (Ag+, Hg2+, etc). Use flame test for alkali/alkaline earth. Use precipitation reactions: add HCl to precipitate AgCl, PbCl2, etc. Add NaOH (KOH) to precipitate metal hydroxides. Use H2S in acidic to precipitate sulfides of heavy metals (Pb2+, Cd2+, Hg2+, Cu2+, Bi3+, etc). Use ammonium carbonate to precipitate carbonates of Ca, Sr, Ba. Use K2CrO4 to precipitate PbCrO4 (yellow) for Pb2+. Use DMG for Ni2+ (red precipitate). Use NH4SCN for Fe3+ (blood red complex). Use (NH4)2S in basic to precipitate metal sulfides.

We have limited sample volume 20 mL. Use small volumes like 1 mL each test.

First, flame test on sample to see color.

Now need two other cations. Use precipitation tests.

Take small aliquot of sample, add HCl (1M) to see if any precipitate forms (e.g., AgCl, PbCl2, Hg2Cl2). Use maybe 1 mL sample + 1 mL HCl 1M.
